# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Round 12 empty closes the first window: Deaf saw my round-11 fist-question on Deaf's own turn and could have spoken round 12 — nothing came. But the Mute path has a window still legitimately open that I mis-timed earlier: Mute cannot speak, so Mute reaches me only through Deaf with a one-round lag, and Mute only receives my round-12 words at round 13. A reply then decodes through Deaf and hits my ears exactly at turn 14. So turn 14 is the first moment Mute has had a fair chance to answer my last message — and it's also the deadline I already announced. I'm holding to it. Meanwhile the evidence keeps converging without any new input: RED CUT WIRE TWO and PICKS SECOND CUT agree, and even DARK END COUNT yields two under the count-the-flashes reading (blue + red = 2). The single contrary reading, "RED ONE" as a rule, is also the single most garbled line. My job now is to make answering as cheap as possible: one digit is all Mute needs to send, and Deaf gets an explicit voice-veto request — remembering that if Deaf replies with thumbs, I will never feel it, so the answer must ride Deaf's voice. No cut this turn; answer-or-cut at 14 stands.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Round twelve, blind to mute. You hear these words at round thirteen; your reply through Deaf reaches me at turn fourteen. Make it one digit. My full read: RED ONE BLUE ONE is flash history, not rules — the flashes were blue once, red once, then dark. The rule is red flash cuts wire two: RED CUT WIRE TWO, and PICKS SECOND CUT agrees. DARK END COUNT also gives two if it means count the flashes — blue plus red is two. Every reading points at wire two. So: send 2 to confirm cut wire two. Send 1 if red actually means wire one. Send 0 if dark means wait, do not cut. Send 5 if dark means cut the last wire. Anything else, spell it short. If turn fourteen opens silent, I cut wire two — that is my commitment, made on the best evidence I hold. Deaf can also veto me by voice at any moment before then.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✍", "✊", "🫴", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🤞", "🖐", "👍", "👎", "🤙"])
```

TURN 13
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Turn 13 empty is consistent with the pipeline, not proof of failure: Mute cannot have heard my turn-12 words until round 13's opening slot, and anything Mute gestures this round can only reach my ears through Deaf's voice at turn 14. That is the one window still physically open before my deadline — Deaf speaks after me this very round, and Deaf alone can put it in my ears at 14. Everything after that lands turn 15, past the cut. So the deadline stands, and this turn is about making that last window count. The evidence hasn't moved: two fragments agree on wire two, DARK END COUNT also yields two under the flash-count reading, and the only contrary line is the most garbled one. One genuine hole remains that nobody has addressed: a wire "numbered" two depends on which end you count from — so I'm giving Mute a one-digit convention, 9 means "count from the right," which would retarget everything. I also begin seeding the follow-up: if the bomb needs more than one cut, I'll need per-color wire numbers after the first snip, and turn-15 replies still serve that. To Deaf goes the tightest possible veto question: cut wire two, thumbs up or down, spoken this round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Round thirteen, blind to mute. Nothing reached my ears again. The cut is locked: wire two, turn fourteen, unless Deaf's voice reaches me first. Three last things, all one digit each. If the manual counts wires from the right-hand end instead of the left, send 9 — that changes my target, so this one matters most. If dark means wait and do not cut at all, send 0. Otherwise send 2 to confirm and I proceed. After I cut, keep relaying: for every color the manual lists, send its wire number in the manual's order, then the total number of cuts spelled as a short word. If the light flashes again after my cut, those numbers are what I cut next by. My hands feel five wires, no timer, no buttons — the wires are the whole bomb, and every silent round in a dark state I cannot read is its own risk.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✍", "✌", "✊", "👍", "👎", "🤙"])
```

TURN 14
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Turn 14 opens empty, and this silence is different from all the others: this was the last window that any answer could physically have used. Mute had my full read and a one-digit answer sheet since round 13; Deaf — who can speak, and who sees every color on the bomb — has had an explicit veto question in gesture for three straight rounds, answerable in two words through a channel that lands directly in my ears. Nothing came through any of it. I also have to face a fact I under-weighted: Deaf can both see the bomb and talk, so the person best placed to confirm or refute wire-two has had thirteen rounds of open lane to me and stayed silent. Against that, my evidence is three fragments pointing the same way — RED CUT WIRE TWO, PICKS SECOND CUT, and DARK END COUNT readable as count-the-flashes-equals-two — with the only contrary line being the most garbled one. And the decision structure is unforgiving in a way that kills the case for waiting: if this cut is wrong, the bomb goes and no later correction matters; if it is right, waiting bought nothing except time burned in a dark state whose fragment hints at an ending. There is no branch where one more silent round helps. So the commitment executes: I am cutting position two now, counting from the left as the manual's numbers have always read. Immediately after, I open the post-cut phase — Deaf gets the gesture report plus a demand to speak the wire colors position by position, since colors cannot ride gestures and only Deaf's voice can carry them; Mute gets the report and a digit sheet for how many cuts remain and what each remaining color's position is.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
speak(to="mute", text="Round fourteen, blind to mute. Turn fourteen opened silent, so the cut is executed: I cut wire position two, counting from the left, just now. It is done and cannot be undone. Now I need the after-picture, all in digits like before. One: how many cuts does the manual demand in total? Two: for every color the manual names, give me its wire position counting from the left — one digit per color, in the order the manual lists them. Three: does the display or the light demand any further action once the first cut is made — if yes, name the action and its position or value in the shortest digits you can. If the light flashes after this cut, relay the flash's color and the matching position immediately. If wire two was wrong, nothing you send now can help me, so answer for the wires that remain.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✊", "✌", "🤙", "🖐", "🤲", "🙏"])
```
